title: PRD addendum: SSO/SAML + RBAC + KMS emergency rotation & audit-schema mapping
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Addendum to the Private Deploy PRD to define deterministic behaviors, acceptance tests, and operator choreography for: (1) SSO/SAML federation corner-cases, (2) RBAC role hierarchy and emergency escalation, (3) audit log schema mapping for customer SIEMs, and (4) emergency KMS/HSM key rotation with zero-downtime fallback. This ticket captures clarified requirements, trade-offs, rollout constraints, and the sign-off checklist needed to unblock Dedicated/Private GA compliance gating.
background: Multiple SOC customers and onboarding teams raised two recurring operational risks during recent pilot onboardings: mismatched audit schema expectations (customer SIEM mapping) and uncertainty about safe key rotation for customer-managed KMS/HSM in private deployments. Earlier PRDs covered high-level goals but deferred deterministic operator behavior. This addendum captures runnable acceptance tests and operator runbook requirements so SREs and enterprise customers can rely on documented, testable behavior.
goals: Define SSO/SAML session expiry and retry semantics for federated IdPs (including SAML relay state recovery).
Lock down RBAC default role-to-permission mapping and describe emergency elevation and audit trail.
Publish an audit-event schema and example transforms for common SIEMs (Splunk, Sumo Logic, Datadog) plus mapping guidance.
Specify KMS/HSM rotation choreography (primary -> staged -> cutover) that preserves active KV caches and allows rollback with a defined SLA.
non_goals: Designing a brand-new proprietary KMS agent — this relies on customer KMS/HSM integrations already scoped in the base PRD.
Full SIEM connector implementation — only schema and example transforms are provided; integrations live in a follow-up implementation ticket.
requirements: SSO: Support SAML 2.0 federation with metadata refresh every 12 hours; validate IdP certificates and surface verification failures to the customer console.
SSO: On SAML authentication failure due to clock skew, attempt one automatic re-auth handshake if signed assertion timestamp is within 2 minutes; log failure reason with error_code=SSO_CLOCK_SKEW.
RBAC: Default role set must include roles: viewer, operator, deployer, owner. Owner role must be the only role allowed to trigger emergency key rotation.
RBAC: Audit logs must include before/after permission deltas for any role change, and the actor principal must be recorded using stable principal_id (not email) for traceability.
Audit logs: Emit structured JSON events with fields: timestamp_utc, event_type, principal_id, resource, outcome, trace_id, meta. Provide sample transform scripts for Splunk HEC and Datadog intake.

KMS/HSM: Key rotation sequence must support 'staged' primary key: new key staged, replication to HSM targets, staged key marked active, consistent cutover window with KV cache warmup, then demote old key after N confirmations. Provide a reversible path within 30 minutes post-cutover.

KMS/HSM: During rotation, requests must automatically fall back to a read path for cached KV entries; writes that cannot encrypt with the active key must queue and be retried after rotation completes, with a bounded queue limit and backpressure metrics exposed.
acceptance_criteria: SAML federation: automated test simulating IdP time skew (±90s) demonstrates single transparent re-handshake and results in an audit event with error_code when handshake fails.
RBAC: Integration test shows role change emitted as two audit events (pre and post) and is retrievable via the console activity API with consistent trace_id.
Audit schema: Given a set of sample events, the provided transform script produces valid Splunk HEC payloads and a mapping README with at least three example SIEM queries per vendor.

KMS rotation: End-to-end test (staging key -> cutover -> rollback) runs in CI using a mocked HSM provider and demonstrates no user-visible 5xx errors; metric assertions: cache_hit_ratio >= 0.85 and rotation_recovery_time <= 30m in the scenario.
Operator runbook: A 10-step operator runbook is reviewed and signed off by SRE and Security with explicit handback criteria; runbook includes 'abort' and 'rollback' decision gates.

Security review: Security engineering approval of threat model and rotation choreography (security@redwood) with mitigations recorded.
SRE review: SRE sign-off on runbook and CI rotation tests (Marcus Liu).

Docs: Console expose schema docs and transform examples in docs.redwood; Docs owner sign-off.
Customer validation: Pilot customer (Acme Finance) validation run completed and feedback captured.
